input: Test the thesis: GLP-1 drug adoption is a lasting volume headwind for Mondelez

output.thesis: GLP-1 drug adoption is a lasting volume headwind for Mondelez

evidence_for.claim: US adoption of GLP-1s has risen sharply. Gallup's National Health and Well-Being Index (5,065 adults) found 11% of US adults currently taking a GLP-1 for weight loss in 2026, up from 3% in 2024. 15% have ever used one, up from 6%. As of July 2026.

Circana (as reported by The Shelby Report) says 30% of US households have a current GLP-1 user, and these households account for 32% of food and beverage units purchased. It projects 40% of units by 2030 if active use reaches 35-40% of households. Spending by GLP-1 households fell 2.5 index points in year one of treatment and 1.9 points in year two, so the drop is lasting rather than a one-off. As of November 2026.

A Cornell/Numerator study of about 150,000 households (Journal of Marketing Research, as reported by RFD-TV) found grocery spending fell 5.3% within six months of starting a GLP-1, and by more than 8% in higher-income households. Savory snacks fell about 10%, with similar pullbacks in sweets, baked goods and cookies. The lower spending lasted at least a year among continuing users, though it moderated.

Cornell/Numerator figures shown by Broadview Capital, via a McKinsey chart: six months after a household adopts a GLP-1, spending is down 7.0% on cookies, 3.5% on candy and chocolate, and 11.5% on chips and savory snacks. Cookies and chocolate are Mondelez's core categories. This measures spending, not units.

Mondelez management itself expects a lasting negative effect, though a small one. On the Q4 2025 call, CEO Van de Put said that over ten years GLP-1s 'could have a 0.5% to 1.5% effect on our overall volumes.'

Mondelez's North American volumes are weak. In Q3 2026, North America volume/mix was flat (0 pp) and organic growth of +1.6% came entirely from pricing. Year to date, North America volume/mix was only +0.2 pp. In Q1 2026 it was -0.4 pp. On the Q4 2025 call, management said the US biscuit category was 'down 4% in volume' over the prior three months.

In Q3 2026, Mondelez recorded brand impairments totaling $64 million. One was a North American biscuits & baked snacks brand, impaired on 'lower expectations of future business performance.' Six brands have fair values within 10% of book value.
FY2025 volume/mix fell 3.7%, versus a 1% decline in 2024. This shows volume was already under pressure as US GLP-1 adoption rose, although management blamed pricing and affordability.

On the Q3 2026 call, the CEO said 'over time, our portfolio needs to evolve towards healthier snacks.' He linked this to the Undercover Snacks acquisition. It suggests management sees a lasting shift in demand.

evidence_against.claim: Volume recovered during 2026. Group volume/mix went from -0.5 pp in Q1 to +0.7 pp in Q2 and +1.8 pp in Q3. Year-to-date volume/mix was +0.6 pp and organic growth +2.4%. Full-year guidance of at least 2% organic growth was reaffirmed. As of Q3 2026.
In Q2 2026, North America volume/mix was +1.2 pp and organic growth +3.4%. That is positive US volume in a year when Gallup put adult GLP-1 use at 11%.

Management sizes the effect at only 0.5%-1.5% of volume over ten years, even with 10-20% US adoption. It said 'we do not see a short-term impact on our business' and called the effect 'almost negligible over a period of ten years.'

Mondelez is mostly exposed outside the US, where GLP-1 adoption is much lower. About 75% of sales come from outside the US (as of 2023). In Q3 2026, North America was $2,846M of $9,967M net revenue (about 29%, my calculation). About 20% of sales were already in snacks under 200 calories (2023).

Mondelez's 2026 filings give other reasons for volume weakness. The Q1 and H1 2026 10-Qs blame pricing elasticity in Europe and Latin America and soft North American biscuit consumption, not GLP-1s. On the Q3 call, the CEO tied North American softness to low consumer confidence 'driven by energy and fuel prices.'

Circana data show some indulgent categories recover. Among GLP-1 households, candy turned positive in the second half of year one and was +5.7 index points in year two. Frozen desserts were +5.3. 81 of 301 subcategories grew in year one and 117 in year two. Meat, cheese and cracker lunch kits were +5.8 in year two.

In Q3 2026, Mondelez gained share in North American biscuits (led by crackers, with Ritz and Ritz Minis) and in candy. Savory biscuits are 'really on a roll.' Global biscuits & baked snacks grew 2.2%, as summarized from call coverage.

counterarguments: Mondelez's own volumes improved while GLP-1 use spread. Group volume/mix went from -0.5 pp in Q1 2026 to +1.8 pp in Q3, with Gallup putting adult use at 11%. That is hard to square with a material, lasting GLP-1 drag.

Most of the business is outside the US: about 71% of Q3 2026 revenue and about 75% of sales per management in 2023. GLP-1 penetration there is much lower, so household-level US declines translate into a small group-level volume effect.

The volume weakness that did happen (FY2025 volume/mix -3.7%, Q1 2026 -0.5 pp) is better explained by cocoa-driven price increases and elasticity, as described in the 10-Qs, plus weak US consumer confidence. Volume recovered once pricing moderated (Q3 pricing was only +0.3 pp).

Circana's year-two data show the drag fading for GLP-1 households: overall spending fell 1.9 points versus 2.5 in year one, and candy turned positive. Portion-controlled formats such as Ritz Minis and sub-200-calorie snacks, plus healthier acquisitions like Undercover Snacks, could limit the damage.
Management's own estimate of 0.5-1.5% of volume over ten years works out to roughly 0.05-0.15 pp a year (my arithmetic). That is lasting but small next to the 3-5% long-term organic growth target.
key_uncertainties: No Mondelez-specific data separate the GLP-1 effect from pricing elasticity and macro softness. Panel data on Mondelez brand purchases by GLP-1 versus non-GLP-1 households would settle this.

Adoption figures disagree: Gallup reports 11% of adults currently using, while Circana reports 30% of households with a current user and 37% ever used. How fast adoption grows from here, given the cheaper oral pills launched in 2026, is unclear. Tracking Gallup, Circana and IQVIA prescription data over time would help.

It is unclear whether GLP-1 households cut cookie and chocolate units for good or come back to them, as Circana found for candy. Circana or Numerator two-year data for cookies, crackers and chocolate would answer this.
International adoption in Europe and emerging markets is unknown. That depends on generic semaglutide arriving as patents expire in some markets, plus reimbursement and pricing outside the US.
North America segment drivers in the Q3 2026 MD&A could not be read from the 10-Q page.
Q4 2026 and 2027 guidance on volume, which management has said it wants to be 'volume-led', is not yet available.
what_would_change_the_view: Mondelez naming GLP-1s as a driver of volume decline in a 10-Q, 10-K or on an earnings call, or raising its estimate above 0.5-1.5% over ten years.

North America volume/mix turning negative again over several quarters while pricing is moderate and consumer confidence stabilizes. That would point to a structural cause rather than an elasticity one.
Circana or Numerator data showing GLP-1 households' unit purchases of cookies, crackers or chocolate falling further in year two or three instead of recovering.
US adult GLP-1 use going well beyond 20% (management's upper scenario), or fast uptake of cheaper oral and generic GLP-1s in Europe and emerging markets.
Strong FY2026 and 2027 volume-led growth that includes positive North America volume/mix. That would weaken the thesis further.
output.verdict: Partly supported, but weak in size. Third-party panel data show GLP-1 households durably cut spending on cookies, sweets and savory snacks, and US adoption has climbed to about 11% of adults (Gallup) and 30% of households (Circana). Management itself expects a lasting 0.5-1.5% volume drag over ten years. For Mondelez, though, the effect is not visible in the reported numbers: group volume/mix improved to +1.8 pp in Q3 2026, about 70% of revenue is outside the US, and the company blames recent volume weakness on pricing elasticity and the macro environment. So the headwind is lasting but small, not a material drag on volume.
